record.paper_title: Open Questions Related to Bose-Einstein Correlations in e+e− → Hadrons
record.context_brief: high inferred energy density of proton and Lambda emitters
record.original_question: How can models of hadron production in electron-positron annihilation account for the approximate minimum emitter energy density inferred from BEC/FDC emitter dimensions being near 100 GeV/fm³ for proton and Lambda emitters, while pion and kaon emitters remain in a reasonable range?

evidence.quote: Consequently one may try and estimate an approximate minimum energy density of the emitter of the two hadrons

Whereas the energy density for the pion and kaon emitters still lies within a reasonable range, the energy densities of the protons and Λ’s emitters are lying in the vicinity of 100 GeV/fm3, way above the values anticipated from the current models for hadron production.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In high-energy electron–positron annihilation into hadrons, identical-boson Bose–Einstein correlations (BEC) and identical-fermion Fermi–Dirac correlations (FDC) between pairs of final-state hadrons can be used to infer an effective spatial size r of the emitting source for each hadron species. From the measured emitter radius r and the typical energy E carried by the emitted hadron, one defines an approximate minimum emitter energy density by

  ρ ≈ E / ((4/3) π r³).

Empirically, when this estimate is applied to pairs of identical pions and identical kaons produced in e⁺e⁻ → hadrons, the resulting energy densities are compatible with values predicted by current models of hadron production. However, when the same procedure is applied to identical-proton and identical-Λ pairs, the inferred emitter energy density is of order 100 GeV/fm³, far exceeding the densities anticipated in any standard model of hadronization in e⁺e⁻ annihilation.

Problem: Construct a model of hadron production in e⁺e⁻ annihilation (or identify a mechanism within an existing framework such as string fragmentation, cluster hadronization, or statistical/thermal hadronization) that reproduces, simultaneously:

(a) the moderate, model-consistent emitter energy densities inferred from BEC measurements of identical-pion and identical-kaon pairs, and

(b) the extremely large (~100 GeV/fm³) emitter energy densities inferred from BEC/FDC measurements of identical-proton and identical-Λ pairs,

and explain physically why baryon emitters appear so much more compact (and thus apparently so much denser) than meson emitters in this analysis.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any publication that resolves the apparent ~100 GeV/fm³ emitter energy density inferred for proton and Λ emitters in e⁺e⁻ → hadrons relative to pion/kaon emitters. Subsequent BEC/FDC studies (e.g., HERMES, LHCb, LEP follow-ups) report source-size measurements but do not appear to provide a definitive hadronization-model explanation of the species-dependent emitter compactness for baryons. The status thus appears unresolved, though no explicit statement to that effect was found.

status_evidence.title: Two scales in Bose–Einstein correlations
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses multiple length scales in BEC source radii without giving a hadronization-model account of the proton/Λ emitter compactness.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature explores multiple BEC scales but does not resolve the baryon emitter density puzzle.

status_evidence.title: The dependence of Bose-Einstein Correlations on energy, multiplicity and hadronic jets
status_evidence.snippet: Studies BEC dependence on event characteristics in e+e- and hadronic collisions.
status_evidence.claim: Later BEC analyses focus on energy/multiplicity dependence rather than reconciling baryon emitter sizes with hadronization models.

status_evidence.title: Three-pion Bose-Einstein correlations measured in proton-proton collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent LHCb measurement of three-pion BEC interpreted in the core-halo model.
status_evidence.claim: Recent BEC work targets mesons in pp; no analogous resolution for proton/Λ emitter density in e+e- is reported.
